summary.intent: Run the full post-execute-phase ship loop for Phase 66 (API schema cutover / publish-gate / tombstone) autonomously through all gates: verify → secure → validate (Nyquist) → simplify → SDK E2E → CodeRabbit CLI → PR creation → review resolution.
summary.outcome: All gates passed and PR #584 was created and pushed. Five fix/hardening commits were added during review (T-66-E1 security fix, tombstone 404 + republish guard, throttle + DTO regex hardening, dead-code cleanup, psql timeouts). Both greptile review threads were resolved. Session ended mid-flow while pushing a CI-required prettier fix for the migration file after the Lint job failed.

repo: Phase 66 deleted all 5 shares spec files (share-invite, share, etc.) without replacing them for the new descriptor-ref model, leaving security-critical claim logic with zero unit coverage post-cutover.
GSD enforcement hooks (verify:post, validate-phase) are disabled in config — gates must be run manually when the ship-phase flow requires them.
Automated GSD executor commits bypass the pre-commit prettier hook; violations surface only in CI `eslint .` (caught the migration file drift).

The 89 sdk-e2e `describe.skip` quarantines carry a `D-01` marker ('SDK runtime stubbed mid-milestone, re-enable at phase 63-65') and predate the branch — any phase touching shares should verify these aren't regressions via `git log` on the test file.

`api:generate` reformats `openapi.json` (single-line → multi-line array expansion) even when the semantic surface is unchanged, producing a cosmetic diff that triggers the api-client pre-commit hook — revert the churn to unblock commits.
The `tombstone` endpoint is the only IPNS controller endpoint missing `@Throttle`; all siblings (publish, batch, unenroll, resolve) have it.

Sibling IPNS DTOs (resolve, tombstone) use the strict `/^k51qzi5uqu5...|bafzaa.../` regex but `create-share.dto` and `create-invite.dto` used the loose `/^k[a-z0-9]+$/` — inconsistency that CodeRabbit flagged.

CodeRabbit CLI false-positives on deleted entities: it reported `FolderIpns` consumers as critical findings because mock-variable names in test files still contained the string, even though the entity symbol was fully removed and the API built and booted cleanly.

code.finding: T-66-E1 security bug: comment claimed 'Write grant is presence-derived from writeDescriptorRef' but code set Share.writeDescriptorRef from dto.writeDescriptorRef without first gating on invite.writeDescriptorRef — a read-only invite could yield a write grant if the claimer supplied the field.

tombstoneRecord discarded the UPDATE's affected-row count and always returned 200, making non-existent, unowned, and already-tombstoned records indistinguishable from successful tombstones (greptile P1).
syncIpnsRecordSequence lacked a tombstonedAt: IsNull() guard in its UPDATE criteria, allowing the republish race window to bump a tombstoned row's sequence (greptile P2).

Spec asserted exact TypeORM update criteria — must be kept in sync when WHERE clause changes (e.g., adding IsNull guards). Required importing IsNull and updating the assertion when the guard was added.
rootIpnsName used loose /^k[a-z0-9]+$/ instead of the canonical strict IPNS-name regex used in sibling DTOs.
Same loose IPNS-name regex as create-share.dto — both needed tightening to match the canonical pattern used by resolve/tombstone DTOs.

Tombstone behavioral tests (404 for unowned/non-existent, 409 for already-tombstoned, success path) were absent and could be inserted after the unenrollBatch describe block using the existing QB mock + mockFolderIpnsRepo.findOne harness.
psql DB-helper functions lacked connection timeouts — CodeRabbit flagged this; adding connect_timeout and statement_timeout to psql invocations prevents silent hangs in CI.

workflow: Adversarially verify subagent results: run the authored spec yourself and confirm no impl files were touched before trusting the GAPS FILLED report.
After gh pr create, the release bot pushes a chore(release) commit; always git fetch + rebase before the next push or it will be rejected.

GitHub GraphQL reply mutations (addPullRequestReviewThreadReply) can timeout silently while the corresponding resolveReviewThread mutation succeeds — re-query reviewThreads afterward and check comment bodies separately to confirm replies actually landed.

CodeRabbit CLI requires a retry on service connection errors; the exit-code-0 result on retry is authoritative — check the full finding count since findings stream incrementally and early reads may be incomplete.
The api:generate semantic-diff check (canonicalized JSON comparison) is the reliable signal for whether a spec actually changed — file-level diff is misleading due to formatting churn.

When CI Lint fails on a committed file, check whether the violation was introduced by an automated commit (GSD executor, release bot) that bypassed local hooks rather than assuming it came from hand-written changes.

friction: GSD verify:post and validate-phase enforcement hooks are disabled in project config — gates must be run manually, adding cognitive overhead to the ship loop.
CodeRabbit CLI hit a service connection error on first run and produced no output; required a blind retry with no indication of which step failed.
OpenAPI generator (api:generate) reformats openapi.json cosmetically even when no surface change occurred, triggering the api-client pre-commit hook and requiring an explicit revert step.
Automated GSD executor commit bypassed the local pre-commit prettier hook, causing a CI Lint failure on the migration file that only surfaced after the PR was pushed.
Background build-chain command timed out on the final git log step, causing a false-negative exit signal — required manual verification via git log.
GitHub GraphQL reply mutations timed out asymmetrically (resolve succeeded, reply did not), requiring a separate re-query and re-post step to confirm thread replies actually landed.
gh pr edit is blocked on this repo by Projects-classic GraphQL; every PR body update requires gh api -X PATCH with a temp file.
The shares module had zero unit specs post-cutover (all 5 deleted, none replaced) — this was a silent gap not caught by any gate until Nyquist ran.
